read: Monday was a strong risk-on session. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% and the Russell 2000 (IWM) 3.2%, but single-stock dispersion in biotech was large: commercial misses and thin early data were punished hard. The day's most important event was Bayer's US approval of Sunharbo (asundexian), the first factor XIa inhibitor to reach market. That gives the sector a validated new anticoagulant class and gives Bayer a needed growth driver. Washington removed WuXi AppTec from the Pentagon's 1260H list, easing a supply-chain overhang for Western sponsors just as Third Rock signed a headline $2bn+ pact with a Chinese AI biologics company. China sourcing remains firmly on. Obesity news flow is still dense but more incremental: Lilly's pill picked up sleep apnoea data, survodutide cleared its CV safety bar with weak tolerability, and FDA added a class-wide NAION warning to GLP-1 labels. Capital keeps going to immunology and neuro, with argenx paying $550m upfront for a peptide platform and Delix raising $100m.

items.headline: Bayer wins FDA approval for Sunharbo (asundexian), the first factor XIa inhibitor, for secondary stroke prevention
items.detail: Approved 9 Nov for patients after a recent non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or high-risk TIA, on the OCEANIC-STROKE data (n=12,327): recurrent ischaemic stroke 6.2% vs 8.4% on placebo (26% RRR), with major bleeding 1.9% vs 1.7% (not significant). Endpoints frames it as a potential blockbuster. It is a first-in-class win for FXIa after years of class setbacks, and it raises the bar for BMS/J&J's milvexian.

items.headline: argenx to acquire private Unnatural Products for up to $1.15bn ($550m upfront)
items.detail: UNP is a macrocyclic peptide company, and BioSpace describes it as a Big Pharma partnering favourite. The deal gives argenx an oral peptide engine alongside its antibody franchise. It is a platform deal rather than a pipeline buy, and it signals that argenx wants oral modalities beyond antibodies.

items.headline: Pentagon removes WuXi AppTec from its Chinese military companies (1260H) list
items.detail: The removal followed a court injunction, though the company could be relisted. WuXi AppTec shares opened more than 6% higher in Hong Kong on Tuesday. This eases a key BIOSECURE-linked overhang for Western sponsors that rely on Chinese CRO/CDMO capacity.

items.headline: Ionis falls about 27% after halving its 2026 Tryngolza sales outlook
items.detail: Ionis now guides Tryngolza to about $50m, from $100-110m, citing a slower launch ramp; Q3 US net sales were $9m. Total Q3 revenue was $243m. The cut puts the sHTG expansion case under pressure, and with it the investment case for Ionis as a commercial company.

items.headline: Lilly's oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron) hits in Phase 3 ATTAIN-OSA; US filing planned before year-end
items.detail: In the 52-week study (n≈712), breathing interruptions fell by up to 44% and up to 32% of patients reached remission or mild disease. Hypoxic burden fell 56% in patients not on PAP. Lilly plans a second OSA label after Zepbound, which widens the pill's comorbidity story against Novo's oral Wegovy.

items.headline: Boehringer/Zealand's survodutide is CV-neutral in SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT (n=5,530); Boehringer to file
items.detail: The trial met non-inferiority on MACE, but GI-driven discontinuation was 19-21% vs 1.9% on placebo, and weight loss was about 13%. William Blair expects approval but sees use confined to patients with liver risk factors. The result is a modest positive for Zealand, and the drug's commercial niche looks MASH-led.

items.headline: FDA orders a class-wide GLP-1 label update adding NAION (optic neuropathy) to Warnings and Precautions
items.detail: The order covers 12 products, including Wegovy, Ozempic, Zepbound, Mounjaro and Foundayo. FDA's meta-analysis found 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 patient-years, and indications are not restricted. BMO sees limited risk to Novo and Lilly, but the change adds to the litigation backdrop.

items.headline: Immunovant up about 15%: IMVT-1402 600mg meets primary endpoint in difficult-to-treat RA
items.detail: In the randomized-withdrawal period, Week 28 ACR20 was 92.5% vs 75.6% on placebo (p=0.014). The 300mg dose failed, and CDAI and SDAI secondaries were not significant. FDA talks on the registrational path come later in 2026, and cash is $722m. This is a cleaner read for FcRn in RA, though the effect relative to the high placebo bar is modest.

items.headline: Vir's elebsiran plus tobevibart meets the primary endpoint in Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 for hepatitis delta
items.detail: 44% of patients reached undetectable HDV with normal ALT, vs 0% in the delayed-treatment arm. Vir targets a mid-2027 filing, and head-to-head data against Gilead's Hepcludex are due next quarter. Shares rose about 12% on Monday.

items.headline: Janux down about 28% on first JANX011 (CD19 TRBV6-engaging TCE) data in healthy volunteers
items.detail: At 3mg, 3 of 5 participants had more than 90% B-cell depletion, with Grade 1 CRS only but one Grade 3 ALT elevation. ITP and RA patient studies start in 2027. The market wanted deeper and more consistent depletion to compete with the crowded autoimmune TCE and CAR-T field.

items.headline: Faeth roughly halves (down about 42%) on Phase 2 PIK-201 data for PIKTOR plus paclitaxel in endometrial cancer
items.detail: In the single-arm study, confirmed ORR was 33% (44% in PIK3CA-mutant patients), with median PFS of 7.4 months. Investors judged this insufficient against current second-line options.

items.headline: Novocure gets an FDA Not Approvable Letter for Optune Mya in NSCLC brain metastases
items.detail: FDA cited uncertainty about the size of the clinical benefit, not safety. Novocure will seek a route to approval without a new trial. This is another hit to the TTFields label-expansion strategy.

items.headline: Third Rock commits up to $2.16bn in a partnership with Chinese AI-biologics company Funnel Biosciences
items.detail: The deal centres on antibody discovery, and the upfront was not disclosed. A US venture firm putting China-sourced discovery at the core of new company creation is a notable escalation of the China trend.

items.headline: Delix Therapeutics raises a $100m Series C for non-hallucinogenic neuroplastogens
items.detail: Delix is trying to catch up with a psychedelics cohort that has re-rated on the Compass filing.

items.headline: Novo-backed Windward Bio sets terms for a US IPO: about 10.3m shares at $16-18 (up to about $185m, about $1bn valuation)
items.detail: The Basel company develops antibodies for asthma, COPD and atopic dermatitis and will list as WWB on Nasdaq. A respiratory and I&I IPO at a $1bn valuation will test how far the IPO window has opened.

items.headline: Oyster Therapeutics (London, formerly Kesmalea) raises a $60m Series A led by 4BIO Capital, with Lilly joining
items.detail: Oyster is developing oral self-assembling degraders that target pathological tau.

items.headline: Heron sells assets to CorMedix for $145m upfront
Compass Pathways completes its FDA submission for COMP360 psilocybin in treatment-resistant depression
items.detail: Compass expects a launch in the first half of next year.

items.headline: J&J/Protagonist's oral IL-23R peptide Icotyde improves psoriatic arthritis in biologic-naive patients
items.detail: Analysts still expect AbbVie's Skyrizi to lead on efficacy.

items.headline: Update: Novartis confirms 9 tumour cases after Zolgensma as FDA investigates, with 2 showing vector integration
items.detail: FDA says benefit-risk remains positive, and the probe extends to Itvisma. This is a class-relevant AAV integration signal.

items.headline: Zura Bio's tibulizumab misses vs placebo in Phase 2 TIBUSHIELD in hidradenitis suppurativa
Roivant: Lisraya books $31m in its first five weeks on the market in dermatomyositis
TG Therapeutics reports Q3 and raises full-year revenue guidance
Endpoints: Trump MFN pricing deals are forcing tough launch-sequencing choices for signatories
items.detail: Companies tagged include Roche, AstraZeneca, Novartis, Lilly and Novo. The issue is ex-US launch timing.

items.headline: Edesa Biotech licenses Japan rights to paridiprubart to Kyorin
